entries.text:
I need help with document export in our reporting page. The export menu offers CSV downloads for the selected rows. The downloaded file sometimes has unexpected header labels, so I started by checking the header row and export settings rather than changing the report itself.

The document export dialog lets me choose a delimiter and an encoding. I tried a comma delimiter and a semicolon delimiter, then opened the downloads in two spreadsheet programs. The exported rows are present, but the column headings look different between downloads. I would like to understand which document export setting controls this result.

There is also a preview of the document before export. The preview shows the selected rows and their headers correctly. Exporting the same selection a second time gives another CSV file with the same values. This makes me suspect something around the export dialog, filename or download settings rather than a missing row in the document.

I checked whether sorting the document changes the exported row order. Sorting changes the preview and the CSV download together. I also checked a small document with a single header and three rows. The export menu, delimiter selector and encoding selector all remain available in that small example.

I can share a sample document and screenshots of the export dialog if needed. The question I originally wrote down was how document export preserves the selected delimiter, encoding and header labels across downloads. Please treat those observations as my report of what I saw, not proof of a cause.
Correction: I described the wrong component. The current problem is connection pooling; available connections are exhausted.

# Document export

Document export creates CSV downloads. Select the delimiter and encoding before export, retain the header row, and verify the downloaded file contains the selected rows. Export settings apply only to the document export component.

# Connection pooling

Connection pooling limits concurrent connections. Inspect pool capacity and release each checked-out connection after use. A connection leak can exhaust available capacity; the pool must not be enlarged without checking resource limits.

# Cache eviction

Cache eviction removes expired cached records. Check the retention interval and invalidation key before changing cache eviction settings.
